title: Non-decreasing Array
summary: An array nums with n integers is to be verified if it can be made non-decreasing by altering at most one element.
statement: An array nums with n integers is to be verified if it can be made non-decreasing by altering at most one element. An array is considered non-decreasing if each element is less than or equal to the next element.
constraints: You may change at most one element to any integer; decide whether the full array can become nondecreasing.
known_wrong_solutions:
def can_be_nondecreasing(nums):
    return sum(a > b for a, b in zip(nums, nums[1:])) <= 1
def can_be_nondecreasing(nums):
    changed = list(nums)
    edits = 0
    for index in range(1, len(changed)):
        if changed[index - 1] <= changed[index]: continue
        edits += 1
        if edits > 1: return False
        changed[index] = changed[index - 1]
    return True
hints: At a violation, either lower the previous value or raise the current one.
Choose the local edit that remains compatible with the value two positions back.
On nums[i-1]>nums[i], lower nums[i-1] if nums[i-2]<=nums[i]; otherwise raise nums[i].
This preserves a nondecreasing processed prefix while spending the only allowed edit as flexibly as possible.
editorial: This preserves a nondecreasing processed prefix while spending the only allowed edit as flexibly as possible.

tests.explanation: One edit cannot repair both decreases.
